methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
AIM Intelligent Machines is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable private companies and 1 public comparable in the robotics sector, spanning seed through Series B stages. Key peers include Humanoid ($1.4B Series A), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), and Dexterity ($1.6B Series B).

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the company's $50M in total raised as a proxy for current value, then applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yielding $100M. The peer-median approach identifies five same-sector comparables at the same or adjacent stage, with a median valuation of $1.6B (range: $1.1B to $2.0B). This method reflects the higher valuations observed among recent Series A and B robotics companies.

Triangulating these two methods produces an implied valuation range of $85M (conservative floor) to $1.9B (high end), with a median of $875M. The wide dispersion between methods reflects fundamental uncertainty about whether AIM should be valued near recent capital deployment ($100M) or anchored to later-stage peer multiples ($1.6B+). Key uncertainties include differentiation relative to the Humanoid and Bedrock comparables, revenue traction relative to Series A peers, and capital efficiency to date. The $875M median represents the midpoint but should be heavily discounted pending clarity on these factors.
